route_structure_note: Edexcel 1RA0 is route-based: students study one Paper 1 religion (1A/1B/1C), a different Paper 2 second religion (2A-2G with restriction that 1B Christianity students cannot take 2A Catholic and vice versa), and then EITHER Paper 3 Philosophy & Ethics (3A/3B/3C, mapped to Paper 1 choice) OR Paper 4 Textual Studies (4A Mark for 1A/1B, 4B Qur'an for 1C). We ship every option as a separate unit so students self-serve via the wizard. Some content (Catholic Christianity Beliefs, Christianity Beliefs, Islam Beliefs, Islam Practices) appears in both Paper 1 and Paper 2 unit families; we ship parallel units rather than reusing rows because Paper 1 contains the additional Sources-of-Wisdom and Forms-of-Expression sections that Paper 2 does not.

article_units.name: Paper 1: Catholic Christianity
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs, practices, sources of wisdom and forms of expression in Catholic Christianity

lessons.title: The Trinity, Creation and Human Nature
lessons.description: The Nicene Creed, the three Persons of God, Catholic creation belief and the dignity of the human person.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Lift Catholic Trinity content from AQA Catholic L1 (Trinity & Nicene Creed). Merge in Genesis creation account material from AQA Catholic L2. Add scriptural anchors used by Edexcel (Matthew 3:13-17 for Trinity, John 1:1-18 for incarnation later). Regenerate practice questions in Edexcel command words (Outline/Explain/Discuss).

lessons.title: Incarnation, Paschal Mystery and Salvation
lessons.description: Jesus as fully God and fully human, the Paschal Mystery, and Catholic belief in salvation and grace.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Lift Incarnation and Redemption content from AQA Catholic L3. Reframe Paschal Mystery (Catholic technical term Edexcel emphasises more than AQA). Keep Luke 24 anchor. Add John 3 / Acts 4 scriptural anchors that Edexcel requires.

lessons.title: Eschatology: Life After Death, Resurrection and Purgatory
lessons.description: Catholic teaching on judgment, heaven, hell and purgatory, including divergent Christian views.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Catholic L4 covers afterlife alongside sacraments; split it cleanly: this lesson is just eschatology. Anchored scriptures John 11 and 2 Cor 5 are Edexcel-specific. Standard 1.8* comparison-marked spec point — students compare with one other tradition in the Discuss question.

lessons.title: Sacraments, the Mass and Catholic Worship
lessons.description: The seven sacraments, the Mass as source and summit, prayer, popular piety and pilgrimage.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Combine AQA Catholic Practices L1 (Prayer & Popular Piety) and L2 (Pilgrimage & Funeral Rite, but only the pilgrimage half). Add the sacramental nature of reality (Catechism 1210-1211) and the Mass as 'source and summit' (Lumen Gentium 7) which Edexcel highlights more explicitly than AQA. The lesson is dense — keep practical worship feel.

lessons.title: Catholic Social Teaching, Mission and Funeral Rite
lessons.description: Justice, peace and reconciliation in Catholic Social Teaching; the work of CAFOD; mission and the funeral rite.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Catholic L3 covers Catholic Social Teaching (CAFOD, love of neighbour). Add Edexcel-specific Evangelii Gaudium references and the funeral rite section. Mission content overlaps with AQA Catholic L4 — merge in.

lessons.title: Sources of Wisdom and Forms of Expression in Catholic Christianity
lessons.description: The Bible, magisterium, the Second Vatican Council, four marks of the Church, plus art, music and architecture as expressions of faith.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. AQA does not have a Sources of Wisdom and Authority section nor a Forms of Expression and Ways of Life section for Catholic Christianity. This is fresh content — Vatican II documents, the four marks of the Church, magisterium, Catholic art/architecture/music/symbolism. Compressed into one dense overview lesson rather than two thin ones (each section has 8 spec bullets but most points are short doctrinal definitions that don't warrant separate lessons).

article_units.name: Paper 1: Christianity
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs, practices, sources of wisdom and forms of expression in Christianity

lessons.title: The Trinity, Creation and the Incarnation
lessons.description: Christian belief in the Trinity, the biblical account of creation and Jesus as the incarnate Son of God.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Christianity Beliefs L1 covers Trinity and nature of God; merge in incarnation from AQA L3. Reframe with Edexcel divergent denominational view (Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant). Use Matthew 3 baptism narrative and John 1:1-18 explicitly — these are the named anchors in 1B.

lessons.title: The Last Days of Jesus, Salvation and Atonement
lessons.description: The Last Supper, crucifixion, resurrection and ascension; Christian beliefs about salvation, grace and atonement.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L3 (Incarnation, Crucifixion, Resurrection) and L4 (Sin, Salvation, Atonement) merge here. Edexcel framing emphasises 'the last days of Jesus' life' as one narrative. Keep Luke 22-24 anchor.

lessons.title: Eschatology and the Problem of Evil
lessons.description: Christian teachings on life after death across denominations, and divergent responses to the problem of evil and suffering.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Christianity Beliefs L2 covers afterlife. Add the problem of evil content (Edexcel 1.7 and 1.8) which AQA places in Theme C. Anchor scriptural references: Psalm 103, Psalm 119, Job. The vale of soul-making framing (Irenaean/Hick) is Edexcel-named.

lessons.title: Christian Worship, Sacraments and Prayer
lessons.description: Liturgical and non-liturgical worship, the role of sacraments in different denominations, and the nature and purpose of prayer.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Lift AQA Christianity Practices L1 (Worship & Prayer) and merge with L2 (Sacraments: Baptism & Holy Communion). Reframe with Edexcel comparison framing (1.6 and 2.1 are starred — students must compare with another tradition). Reference Pentecostal less-structured worship which is named in 1B 2.1.

lessons.title: Pilgrimage, Festivals and the Church in the Community
lessons.description: Pilgrimage to Jerusalem, Iona, Taize and Walsingham; Christmas and Easter; mission, the local church and Christian Aid.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Lift AQA Christianity Practices L3 (Pilgrimage & Festivals) and L4 (Mission, Evangelism, Worldwide Church). Iona and Taize are Edexcel-named pilgrimage sites that AQA does not mention. Christian Aid (1B 2.8) replaces AQA's Trussell Trust framing.

lessons.title: Sources of Wisdom and Forms of Expression in Christianity
lessons.description: The Bible, denominations, leadership and the role of women, plus Christian art, icons, drama, literature and music.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. AQA has no Sources of Wisdom or Forms of Expression sections in its Christianity papers. Sources covers Bible authority, denominations (Catholic/Orthodox/Protestant/Pentecostal growth and Filioque/Reformation), leadership and the role of women — fresh content. Forms of Expression covers paintings (with two named pieces), icons, sculpture, symbolism, drama, literature (CS Lewis is spec-named), traditional and contemporary music (Gregorian Chant, Graham Kendrick, Casting Crowns). Both 8 spec bullets each. Densely packed into one overview lesson.

article_units.name: Paper 1: Islam
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs, practices, sources of wisdom and forms of expression in Islam

lessons.title: The Nature of Allah and Core Muslim Beliefs
lessons.description: Tawhid, the Six Beliefs of Islam, the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam, and the characteristics of Allah.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Merge AQA Islam Beliefs L1 (Core Beliefs: Six Articles & Five Roots) and L2 (Tawhid & Nature of Allah). Edexcel surfaces Sevener vs Twelver in Shi'a — keep that. Reference Surah 16:35-36 explicitly (Edexcel-named anchor).

lessons.title: Risalah, Holy Books, Angels and Predestination
lessons.description: Prophets including Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad; the Qur'an and other holy books; angels Jibril, Izra'il and Mika'il; al-Qadr.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Islam Beliefs L3 (Risalah, Holy Books, Prophethood) covers most of this. Add angels (AQA places this in L2) and al-Qadr (AQA L4). Edexcel asks for explicit Surah anchors per spec point.

lessons.title: Akhirah: Life After Death and the Day of Judgement
lessons.description: Muslim teaching on judgment, paradise and hell, and how belief in the afterlife shapes Muslim life.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Islam Beliefs L4 covers al-Qadr alongside Akhirah; here we lift just the Akhirah half. Edexcel 1.8* is the starred comparison spec point (students must compare with another tradition in the Discuss question). Anchor Surah 17:49-72.

lessons.title: The Five Pillars and Ten Obligatory Acts
lessons.description: Shahadah, Salah, Sawm, Zakah and Hajj; the Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam; Khums.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Islam Practices spans 4 lessons; merge L1 (Five Pillars & Shahadah), L2 (Salah & Sawm), L3 (Zakah & Hajj). The Ten Obligatory Acts and Khums are Shi'a-specific and Edexcel-named explicitly. Practice & Significance of Worship (2.3*) is starred — comparison question target.

lessons.title: Jihad and Islamic Festivals
lessons.description: Lesser and greater Jihad; Id-ul-Adha, Id-ul-Fitr, Id-ul-Ghadeer and Ashura.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Islam Practices L4 covers Jihad & Islamic Festivals. Edexcel adds Id-ul-Ghadeer (Shi'a) which AQA does not specifically name; cover it with a couple of paragraphs. Care needed: lesser/greater Jihad framing must be doctrinally accurate — never reduce to 'inner struggle vs holy war' caricature. Edexcel examiners flag this misconception.

lessons.title: Sources of Authority and Muslim Identity
lessons.description: The Qur'an, the Prophet Muhammad, Hadith, Shari'ah Law and Sufism; mosque architecture, calligraphy, Muslim identity and charity.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. AQA Islam papers have no Sources of Wisdom or Forms of Expression sections. Densely packed: Qur'an + Prophet + Hadith + Shari'ah + Imamate (Section 3) plus mosque + calligraphy + Sufism + halal/haram + Muslim charity (Section 4). 16 spec bullets in one lesson — treat as a sweep with strong sub-headings. Important: Sufi figures al-Ghazali, ibn al-Arabi and Rabi'a al-Adawiyya are named — get their bios right (al-Ghazali's 'Revival of Religious Sciences' is a real text).

article_units.name: Paper 2: Catholic Christianity
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and practices of Catholic Christianity as the second religion

lessons.title: Catholic Beliefs: Trinity, Incarnation and Creation
lessons.description: The Trinity, the biblical creation account, the dignity of the human person and the Incarnation.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Same content as Paper 1 Catholic L1 but compressed (Paper 2 has no Sources/Forms sections, less overall content needed). AQA Catholic L1+L2 source. Frame the lesson assuming the student's main religion is Christianity or Islam — context bridge in intro.

lessons.title: Paschal Mystery, Salvation and Eschatology
lessons.description: Catholic teaching on Jesus' death and resurrection, salvation and grace, and Catholic beliefs about the afterlife and purgatory.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Catholic L3+L4 source — Incarnation and Redemption + Life After Death. 1.8* is the comparison-marked spec point.

lessons.title: Sacraments, the Mass and Catholic Prayer
lessons.description: The sacramental nature of reality, the seven sacraments, the Mass as source and summit, and forms of Catholic prayer.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Catholic Practices L1 source. 2.2* is the worship-comparison-marked spec point. Mass framing must reference 'source and summit' (Lumen Gentium 7) — Edexcel-named.

lessons.title: Pilgrimage, Catholic Social Teaching and Mission
lessons.description: Catholic pilgrimage, Catholic Social Teaching with CAFOD, the funeral rite and Catholic mission and evangelism.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Catholic Practices L2+L3+L4 source. Combine pilgrimage, funeral rite, social teaching and mission. Less depth than Paper 1 Catholic L4-L5 since Paper 2 is 25% weighting.

article_units.name: Paper 2: Christianity
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and practices of Christianity as the second religion

lessons.title: Christian Beliefs: God, Creation and Jesus
lessons.description: The Trinity, the creation accounts, the Incarnation and the last days of Jesus' life.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Christianity Beliefs L1+L3+L4. Comparable compression to Paper 2 Catholic L1.

lessons.title: Eschatology and the Problem of Evil
lessons.description: Christian beliefs about life after death and divergent responses to suffering and evil.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L2 source. 1.6* is the comparison-marked spec point. Problem of evil treated more concisely than Paper 1 Christianity L3.

lessons.title: Christian Worship, Sacraments and Prayer
lessons.description: Liturgical and non-liturgical worship, baptism and Eucharist across denominations, and forms of Christian prayer.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Christianity Practices L1+L2 source. 2.1* worship comparison-marked.

lessons.title: Pilgrimage, Festivals, Mission and the Worldwide Church
lessons.description: Pilgrimage sites, Christmas and Easter, mission and evangelism, the local church and Christian Aid.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L3+L4 source. Iona and Taize are Edexcel-specific pilgrimage sites.

article_units.name: Paper 2: Islam
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and practices of Islam as the second religion

lessons.title: Core Muslim Beliefs and the Nature of Allah
lessons.description: Tawhid, the Six Beliefs, the Five Roots of Shi'a Islam, Risalah and the Holy Books.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Islam Beliefs L1+L2+L3 source. Compressed.

lessons.title: Angels, Predestination and Akhirah
lessons.description: Malaikah, al-Qadr and Muslim teaching on life after death.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L4 (Al-Qadr, Akhirah, Day of Judgement) source. Add angels (Edexcel groups them here). 1.8* is the afterlife comparison-marked spec point.

lessons.title: The Five Pillars and Ten Obligatory Acts
lessons.description: Shahadah, Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Hajj, the Ten Obligatory Acts and Khums.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Islam Practices L1+L2+L3 source. 2.3* Salah is comparison-marked.

lessons.title: Jihad and Islamic Festivals
lessons.description: Lesser and greater Jihad and the major Islamic celebrations including Id-ul-Adha, Id-ul-Fitr and Ashura.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L4 source. Same content as Paper 1 Islam L5 — students rotating through paper 1 vs paper 2 will see consistent material.

article_units.name: Paper 2: Buddhism
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and practices of Buddhism as the second religion

lessons.title: The Buddha, the Dhamma and the Three Marks of Existence
lessons.description: The life of the Buddha, the Four Sights, dependent origination and the three marks of dukkha, anicca and anatta.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Buddhism Beliefs L1 (Dhamma, Three Marks) and L3 (Buddha & Four Noble Truths). Edexcel explicitly names Buddhavamsa XXVI and the Story of Nagasena/Milinda Panha as anchor texts. Combine L1+L3 because Edexcel groups the Buddha's life with the Three Marks under 2D 1.1-1.2.

lessons.title: The Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path
lessons.description: The Four Noble Truths, samudaya, the cessation of tanha, nibbana and the Eightfold Path / Threefold Way.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA L3+L4 source. Edexcel breaks Four Noble Truths into four spec bullets — each Sutta-anchored. 1.5* is the comparison-marked spec point (afterlife/cessation framing).

lessons.title: Human Life, Ethics and Worship in Buddhism
lessons.description: Five Khandas, sunyata, Arahant and Bodhisattva ideals, the Five Precepts, kamma, metta, and Buddhist meditation.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Buddhism Beliefs L2 (Human Personality & Destiny) and L4 (Eightfold Path & Ethics) plus Buddhism Practices L2 (Meditation). Compressed.

lessons.title: Buddhist Worship: Temples, Puja, Death Rites and Festivals
lessons.description: Buddhist places of worship, buddharupas, puja in vihara and home, death and mourning rituals, and major festivals.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Buddhism Practices L1+L3+L4 source. Edexcel names specific Suttas as anchors (Kimsila, Vakkali, Mangala, Anapanasati). 2.6* puja comparison-marked. Edexcel-specific festivals: Hanamatsuri (Japanese), Lama Tsong Khapa Day (Tibetan) — these are named in 2.8.

article_units.name: Paper 2: Hinduism
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and practices of Hinduism as the second religion

lessons.title: Brahman, the Three Aspects of the Divine and the Deities
lessons.description: Brahman as Nirguna and Saguna, the three aspects (Brahman, Antaryami, Bhagavan), and the major deities including Vishnu, Shiva and Shakti.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Hinduism Beliefs L1+L2 source. Edexcel-named scriptural anchors (Katha Upanishad 2.2.6-8, Mundaka Upanishad 2.1, Rig Veda 1.154.1-2). Antaryami (within the heart) is an Edexcel-emphasised concept.

lessons.title: Atman, Samsara and the Purpose of Life
lessons.description: The atman, karma, the cycle of samsara, moksha, the four aims of life and varnashrama dharma.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Hinduism Beliefs L3+L4. 1.5* (life-after-death) comparison-marked. Edexcel uses the term 'anatana dharma' for eternal law — AQA uses 'sanatana'. Use Edexcel spelling.

lessons.title: Suffering, Cosmology and Hindu Worship
lessons.description: Hindu responses to suffering, Hindu cosmology including the yugas and maya, and forms of Hindu worship and yoga.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Hinduism Practices L1+L4 partial source — covers yoga, puja and home/mandir worship. Hindu cosmology (yugas, maya, prakriti, tri-guna) is mostly AQA-light — Edexcel asks for explicit treatment with Rig Veda 10.129 anchor. Medium because the cosmological framework is genuinely more developed in Edexcel.

lessons.title: Hindu Festivals, Pilgrimage and Charity
lessons.description: Diwali, Holi and other festivals, pilgrimage to the Ganges and sacred sites, environmental projects and Hindu charity work.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Hinduism Practices L3 (Diwali, Holi) and L4 (yogas, pilgrimage, charities). Edexcel names more festivals than AQA (Ram Navami, Ratha-yatra, Janmashtami, Raksha Bandhan). Environmental projects (cow protection) is Edexcel-emphasised.

article_units.name: Paper 2: Judaism
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and practices of Judaism as the second religion

lessons.title: The Nature of God, Shekhinah and the Messiah
lessons.description: The Almighty as One, Creator, Law-Giver and Judge; the Shekhinah; and Jewish beliefs about the Messiah.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Judaism Beliefs L1+L2 source. Edexcel specifies 'the Almighty' as the formal title (AQA uses 'God'). Anchor 2 Chronicles 7:1-3 for Shekhinah and Jeremiah 23:5-8 for Messiah.

lessons.title: The Covenant and Jewish Moral Principles
lessons.description: The Abrahamic covenant, the Sinai Covenant and the Ten Commandments, sanctity of life and Pikuach Nefesh, the Mitzvot, and Jewish beliefs about life after death.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Judaism Beliefs L3 (Covenant) and L4 (Moral Principles & Pikuach Nefesh). Maimonides' Mishneh Torah Sefer Madda is Edexcel-named. 1.8* afterlife comparison-marked.

lessons.title: Jewish Worship: Synagogue, Prayer and Sacred Texts
lessons.description: Public worship in the synagogue, the Tenakh and Talmud, food laws, prayer at home, and the Shema and Amidah.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Judaism Practices L1+L2 source. 2.4* Shema/Amidah comparison-marked. Edexcel specifically names Deuteronomy 6:4 as anchor and the Mezuzah.

lessons.title: Family Life, Shabbat, Festivals and the Synagogue
lessons.description: Birth rituals, Bar/Bat Mitzvah, marriage and mourning; Shabbat; Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, Pesach, Shavuot and Sukkot; features of the synagogue.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Judaism Practices L3 (Family Life) + L4 (Dietary Laws & Festivals) + L1 (Synagogue features). Edexcel anchors: Exodus 27:20-21 for ner tamid, Proverbs 14:28 for synagogue layout.

article_units.name: Paper 2: Sikhism
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and practices of Sikhism as the second religion

lessons.title: The Nature of God and Human Life in Sikhism
lessons.description: God in the Mool Mantar, God as Creator, the purpose of human life and the path to mukti.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Sikhism Beliefs L1+L2 source. Edexcel emphasises Guru Granth Sahib citations by page number — keep AQA's usage. 1.4* afterlife comparison-marked.

lessons.title: Gurmukh, Equality, Sewa and the Sangat
lessons.description: Being gurmukh and eliminating haumai, the oneness of humanity and gender equality, sewa, and the importance of the sangat.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Sikhism Beliefs L3 (Oneness & Equality) + L4 (Sewa & Sangat) + L2 partial (Sikh Virtues). Mai Bhago is Edexcel-named — keep her as named example of women's leadership.

lessons.title: The Gurdwara, Langar and Daily Worship
lessons.description: Features of the gurdwara, langar, Nam Japna and Sikh daily prayer.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Sikhism Practices L1+L2 source. 2.5* prayer comparison-marked. The four doors of the gurdwara (signifying openness to all castes/genders) is Edexcel-emphasised.

lessons.title: Akhand Path, Gurpurbs and Sikh Ceremonies
lessons.description: The Akhand Path, gurpurbs including Guru Nanak's birthday and Vaisakhi, Divali, and birth and naming ceremonies including Amrit Sanskar.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Sikhism Practices L3 (Festivals, Birth) + L4 (Amrit Sanskar, Khalsa, Five Ks) source. Edexcel-specific: Guru Tegh Bahadur martyrdom commemoration. Names Singh/Kaur convention — covered same way as AQA.

article_units.name: Paper 3: Philosophy and Ethics (Catholic)
article_units.subtitle: Arguments for the existence of God and Catholic teaching on relationships and families

lessons.title: Revelation, Visions and Miracles as Proof of God
lessons.description: Revelation through Jesus, biblical and non-biblical visions, miracles at Lourdes, and atheist and Humanist counter-arguments.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L3 (Revelation: Visions, Miracles, Nature) is the closest match but AQA is religion-agnostic. Edexcel 3A is Catholic-specific — examples must be Catholic (Joan of Arc visions, miracles at Lourdes are Edexcel-named). Frame around Catholic doctrinal positions, not generic theism. Medium transferability because the spec content is the same arguments but the religion-specific framing requires rework.

lessons.title: Religious Experience, the Design Argument and the Cosmological Argument
lessons.description: Religious experience as evidence for God, the classical design argument, and Aquinas's first three Ways.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L1+L2 (For and Against). Aquinas's First Three Ways are Edexcel-named explicitly — important fact-check anchor: Aquinas has Five Ways total, Edexcel specifies the first three (motion, causation, contingency). Don't conflate with the Ontological Argument (not in Edexcel 3A). Romans 1:18-24 is the Catholic-named anchor.

lessons.title: The Problem of Evil and Catholic Responses
lessons.description: How suffering challenges belief in an all-loving God, and Catholic responses including Augustine's free-will defence and Irenaean soul-making.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L2 (Arguments Against). Augustine's free-will defence and Irenaean soul-making (via John Hick) are Edexcel-named — fact-check anchor: Augustine attributed evil to the misuse of free will; Irenaeus (developed by John Hick) attributed evil's purpose to soul-making. Don't conflate these — common student error. Frame Catholic-specifically with reference to Psalm 119/Job.

lessons.title: Marriage, Sexual Relationships and Family
lessons.description: Catholic teaching on marriage as a sacrament, sexual relationships as marital, unitive and procreative, and the purpose of families in the 21st century.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme A L1+L2 source. Edexcel-specific: papal document Familiaris Consortio (1981, John Paul II) named explicitly; 'Not Just Good But Beautiful' (Pope Francis address) named. The marital/unitive/procreative framing is Catholic-canonical and should not be paraphrased — these are technical terms in Edexcel mark schemes.

lessons.title: Contraception, Divorce, Gender Equality and Discrimination
lessons.description: Catholic teaching on contraception and Humanae Vitae, divorce and annulment, the equality of men and women in the family, and Catholic opposition to gender prejudice.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme A L2 (Families, Gender, Equality) + L3 (Contraception, Same-Sex). Humanae Vitae is Edexcel-named — fact-check anchor: published 1968 by Pope Paul VI, prohibits artificial contraception. Theology of the body is John Paul II's catechesis series 1979-1984. Situation ethics (Joseph Fletcher) named as a contrast ethical theory.

article_units.name: Paper 3: Philosophy and Ethics (Christianity)
article_units.subtitle: Arguments for the existence of God and Christian teaching on relationships and families

lessons.title: Revelation, Visions and Miracles
lessons.description: Christian belief in revelation through the Bible and Jesus, visions, miracles and Humanist counter-arguments.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L3 (Revelation). Edexcel 3B uses Noah/Abraham covenants as revelation framework (3B 1.1) — Christianity-general rather than Catholic-specific. Less doctrinal weight than 3A.

lessons.title: Religious Experience, Prayer, Design and Cosmological Arguments
lessons.description: Religious experience as proof of God, the role of answered prayer, the design argument and the cosmological argument.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L1+L2 source. Edexcel 3B includes prayer as a separate spec point (3B 1.5) — pray-then-receive framing from 1 John 5. The cosmological argument is non-Catholic here (no Aquinas-specific naming) but Aquinas's First Three Ways still apply as the canonical statement.

lessons.title: Religious Upbringing as an Argument
lessons.description: Christian teaching on raising children to believe in God; how religious upbringing might lead to or away from belief.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. AQA does not treat religious upbringing as a discrete argument-for-existence point. Standalone short lesson covering Proverbs 22:6 ('Train up a child') and the indoctrination counter-argument from Dawkins. Could be merged with L2 — kept separate so 3B has full 5-lesson coverage matching 3A. NOTE: Edexcel 3B does not include the problem of evil under Section 1 (unlike 3A 1.7-1.8), so this slot replaces problem-of-evil coverage.

lessons.title: Marriage, Sexual Relationships and Family
lessons.description: Christian teaching on marriage, sexual relationships and the purpose of the family, and the support of the local parish.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme A L1+L2 source. Christianity-general framing (Catholic, Protestant and other divergent positions). Mark 10:6-9 is the canonical scriptural anchor.

lessons.title: Contraception, Divorce, Gender Equality and Discrimination
lessons.description: Christian views on family planning, divorce and remarriage, the equality of men and women, and Christian opposition to gender prejudice.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme A L2+L3 source. Christianity-general. Galatians 3:23-29 ('neither male nor female') is the standard Pauline anti-discrimination anchor. Matthew 19:1-12 for divorce.

article_units.name: Paper 3: Philosophy and Ethics (Islam)
article_units.subtitle: Arguments for the existence of Allah and Muslim teaching on relationships and families

lessons.title: Revelation, Visions and Miracles in Islam
lessons.description: The Qur'an as revelation, visions in Islam, the Qur'an as a miracle, and Humanist counter-arguments.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L3 source. Reframe for Islam: the Qur'an is itself the miracle (Surah 17:84-89, the 'challenge' verses). Surah 19:16-22 covers the Maryam (Mary) vision. Different scriptural anchors throughout — significant adaptation.

lessons.title: Religious Experience, Design and Cosmological Arguments
lessons.description: Religious experience in Sunni, Shi'a and Sufi traditions, the design argument, and the kalam cosmological argument from al-Ghazali.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L1 (Arguments For). Edexcel 3C is Islamic-specific: al-Ghazali's kalam cosmological argument (real text Kitab al-lqtisad fil'ltiqad). Fact-check anchor: al-Ghazali (1058-1111 CE), kalam = 'speech' or 'rational theology'. Kalam argument: everything that begins to exist has a cause; the universe began to exist; therefore the universe has a cause. Don't conflate with Aquinas — kalam is distinct.

lessons.title: The Problem of Suffering in Islam
lessons.description: How suffering challenges belief in Allah as compassionate, and Muslim responses including life as a test, prayer and charity.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme C L2 source. Reframe with Islamic theological response: life as a test (dunya as imtihaan), patience (sabr) as a key virtue, prayer and charity as practical responses. Don't import Augustine/Irenaean theodicies — Islam has its own theological framework here.

lessons.title: Marriage, Sexual Relationships and Family in Islam
lessons.description: Muslim teaching on marriage, sexual relationships, family life and the support of the ummah.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme A L1 source. Reframe for Islam with Surah 4 (An-Nisa, 'the Women') as the central scriptural reference. Strengthening of the ummah is an Islamic-specific framing for family purpose.

lessons.title: Contraception, Divorce, Gender Equality and Discrimination
lessons.description: Muslim teaching on contraception, divorce and remarriage, the role of men and women in the family, and Muslim views on gender prejudice.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: AQA Theme A L2+L3 source. Reframe with Hadith and Qur'an anchors. Fact-check: Surah 33:35 explicitly lists equality of religious duties for men and women — important for the equality discussion. Talaq divorce procedures differ between Sunni (three pronouncements) and Shi'a (single pronouncement plus witnesses) — Edexcel-named in 2.6.

article_units.name: Paper 4: Mark's Gospel
article_units.subtitle: Who Jesus is and the nature of discipleship as shown in the Gospel of Mark

lessons.title: Jesus as Messiah, Son of Man and the Baptism
lessons.description: Old Testament expectations of the Messiah, the title Son of Man in Mark and Daniel, and the baptism of Jesus.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. AQA does not have a textual studies paper. Generate fresh from spec and named Mark passages. Fact-check anchors: Daniel 7:13 is the canonical Son of Man passage in the Old Testament; Mark 1:2-11 is the baptism passage; Isaiah 53 is the Suffering Servant passage which Christians read as messianic. Care needed: 'Son of Man' has dual referents — in Daniel it's apocalyptic, in Mark Jesus uses it self-referentially.

lessons.title: Miracles of Jesus in Mark
lessons.description: Nature miracles (the calming of the storm, the feeding of the 5,000, walking on water) and healing miracles (Legion, Jairus's daughter), and what they show about Jesus.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Fresh content covering five named Mark passages. Fact-check: the feeding of the 5,000 (Mark 6:32-44) is one of two feeding miracles in Mark; don't confuse with the 4,000 (Mark 8). Legion = the Gerasene demoniac. Jairus was a synagogue ruler. All passages are real and accurately verse-numbered in the spec — preserve them.

lessons.title: Peter's Confession, the Transfiguration and Conflicts of Jesus
lessons.description: Peter's confession at Caesarea Philippi, the messianic secret, the Transfiguration, and Jesus's conflicts with religious authorities.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Fact-check: 'Elias' is Edexcel's archaic transliteration of Elijah — the spec uses 'Elias' so respect that. The messianic secret is a real scholarly motif identified by William Wrede (1901). The Transfiguration features Moses (the lawgiver) and Elijah (the prophet). Cleansing of the Temple is in Mark 11:15-18 — happens in Mark immediately after the triumphal entry.

lessons.title: The Last Days of Jesus and the Passion
lessons.description: The arrest, Last Supper, Gethsemane, trials before the High Priest and Pilate, the crucifixion and the resurrection.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Fact-check: Mark 16:1-8 is the original ending of Mark — the women find the empty tomb and flee in fear. Verses 9-20 are the 'longer ending' which most scholars consider a later addition; this lesson should reference Mark 16:1-8 as the spec does. Pilate's trial is in Mark 15:1-15; the Sanhedrin (High Priest) trial is in Mark 14:53-65. Don't conflate the two trials.

lessons.title: Discipleship: The Call, the Cost and Living It Today
lessons.description: The call of the disciples, parables about discipleship (Tenants, Sower, Rich Man), Peter's denial, women in the Gospel, and discipleship today (Bonhoeffer, Romero or Mother Teresa).

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Heavy lesson — 8 spec bullets crammed in. Fact-check anchors: Dietrich Bonhoeffer (1906-1945), German Lutheran pastor executed by the Nazis for plotting against Hitler, author of 'The Cost of Discipleship' (1937). Oscar Romero (1917-1980), Archbishop of San Salvador, assassinated while saying Mass for defending the poor against the military junta. Mother Teresa (1910-1997), Albanian-Indian Catholic nun, founder of Missionaries of Charity, canonised 2016. Mark 8:34 is 'whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me' — this is the verse Bonhoeffer titled his book around. The anointing at Bethany is Mark 14:3-9 (an unnamed woman with the alabaster jar). The Greek (Syrophoenician) woman is Mark 7:25-30. The rich man story is Mark 10:17-31 ('it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle').

article_units.name: Paper 4: The Qur'an
article_units.subtitle: Beliefs and teachings of Islam and the lives of the prophets and others in the Qur'an

lessons.title: Allah in the Qur'an: Al-Fatiha, Tawhid and the 99 Names
lessons.description: The opening surah and the way Allah is described, the oneness of Allah in Surah al-Anaam, and the 99 beautiful names.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Fresh content. Fact-check: Surah al-Fatiha (Surah 1) is the 'Opening' — 7 verses, recited in every prayer cycle. Surah al-Anaam (Surah 6) is 'The Cattle'. The 99 names are real — Edexcel selects six specific ones with named verse anchors. Translate them accurately: Ar-Rahman = the All-Merciful, Ar-Rahim = the All-Merciful (different shade of mercy — Rahman is universal, Rahim is specific), As-Salam = Source of Peace, Al-Khaliq = the Creator, Al-Ghaffar = the All-Forgiving, Ar-Razzaq = the Sustainer.

lessons.title: Believers, Creation and Humanity as Khalifah
lessons.description: How believers are described in Surah al-Baqarah, the Qur'anic creation account and humanity as vicegerent/khalifah.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Surah al-Baqarah is Surah 2, the longest in the Qur'an. Khalifah/khalifa = 'successor' or 'vicegerent' — humans as Allah's stewards on Earth. Surah 2:30-39 is the Adam-and-angels narrative where Allah declares Adam as khalifah and the angels question this.

lessons.title: Justice, Shirk and Shari'ah Law
lessons.description: The nature of justice in Surah An-Nisa, the prohibition of shirk, and the role of Shari'ah law.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Shirk = associating partners with Allah (the cardinal sin in Islam). Surah 7:148-150 is the Golden Calf episode (referenced in 4B 1.7). Surah An-Nisa = Surah 4, 'The Women'. Shari'ah = 'path' or 'way' — the religious law derived from Qur'an + Sunnah.

lessons.title: The Prophets: Nuh, Ibrahim, Ismail and Yusuf
lessons.description: The lives and teachings of the prophets Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Ismail and Yusuf (Joseph) in the Qur'an.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Fact-check: Surah 71 ('Nuh') is one of the shorter surahs entirely devoted to Noah. Surah 12 ('Yusuf') is the only surah devoted entirely to one prophet's story. The Islamic narrative of the sacrifice differs from the Biblical: in the Qur'an, the son to be sacrificed is traditionally identified as Ismail (not Isaac as in Genesis 22), though the Qur'an does not name him directly — the spec notes 'possible debate about which son'. Ibrahim built the Ka'ba with Ismail (Surah 2:127-129).

lessons.title: Dawud, Maryam, Isa and the Mission of Muhammad
lessons.description: The Prophet Dawud and the Zabur, Maryam and the birth of Isa, the life and mission of Isa, and the preaching of Muhammad.

content_transfer.adaptation_notes: Edexcel-specific. Fact-check: Surah 19 ('Maryam') is named after Mary and tells of the annunciation by Jibril (Gabriel) and the virgin birth of Isa. Islamic teaching on Isa's death is distinct from Christianity — Surah 4:157-158 says 'they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them' — most Muslim scholars read this as Allah raising Isa to heaven before crucifixion. This must be presented respectfully and accurately — both the Islamic position and the Christian-Muslim divergence on this point. Surah 61:6 has Isa foretelling Ahmad/Muhammad. Surah 26:213-217 is Muhammad's command to preach to his clan.

question_type_naming_notes: Edexcel 1RA0 uses a specific four-part question format per topic: (a) Outline three (3 marks, AO1, factual recall), (b) Explain two (4 marks, AO1, understanding beyond habitual response), (c) Explain two with reference to a source of wisdom or authority (5 marks, AO1, with one named source citation), (d) Discuss a statement (12 marks plus 3 marks SPaG on selected questions, AO2, evaluative judgement with reasoned chain). 'Describe' (3 marks) is used in some papers as a near-synonym for 'Outline'. Names omit paper codes per copyright rules — no '1RA0/1A' or 'Paper 1' in user-facing strings. The 12-mark Discuss is the highest-stakes question and what Pearson's training and exemplar materials focus most heavily on.

common_misconceptions.topic: Lesser vs greater Jihad in Islam
common_misconceptions.misconception: Students often reduce Jihad to 'holy war' or oversimplify the greater/lesser distinction as 'inner struggle vs holy war'. Greater Jihad is the spiritual struggle against the lower self (nafs); lesser Jihad is defensive struggle in specific conditions (e.g. Surah 2:190-194). The conditions for declaration of lesser Jihad are tightly constrained in classical Islamic jurisprudence.
common_misconceptions.source: NATRE research on teaching about Islam (Picturing Islam, Picturing Muslims project, RE Today/NATRE) — teachers' confidence in teaching Islam is uneven and 'theology vs everyday lived Islam' is a frequent gap.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students conflate Aquinas's First Three Ways (motion, causation, contingency) with the Ontological Argument or with the Kalam Cosmological Argument. They are distinct: Aquinas's first three ways are a posteriori arguments from features of the world; the Ontological Argument (Anselm) is a priori and not in Edexcel 1RA0 Paper 3; Kalam (al-Ghazali) is the Islamic version in Paper 3C.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson Edexcel 1RA0 specification — Aquinas First Three Ways named explicitly in 3A 1.6 and 3B 1.7; Kalam in 3C 1.6 with al-Ghazali named.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students confuse Augustine's free-will defence (evil as the privation of good, caused by misuse of free will, the Fall) with Irenaean soul-making (evil as a necessary feature for moral and spiritual development, developed in the modern era by John Hick). Both are Edexcel-named in 3A 1.8 and feed into 1B 1.8 problem-of-evil content.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson Edexcel 1RA0 spec, 3A 1.8 names St Augustine and St Irenaeus by name.

common_misconceptions.topic: Catholic vs general Christian framing in Paper 3
common_misconceptions.misconception: Paper 3A students writing on the Paper 3B (general Christianity) framing or vice versa. The Catholic paper (3A) requires references to Catechism paragraphs, papal documents (Humanae Vitae, Familiaris Consortio, Evangelii Gaudium, Not Just Good But Beautiful) and Magisterium teaching specifically. 3B Christianity is denomination-wide.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson 1RA0 spec — 3A explicitly references Catechism numbers throughout; 3B does not.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students cite the 'longer ending' (Mark 16:9-20) as the canonical resurrection account in Mark. The spec specifies Mark 16:1-8 (the empty tomb, women fleeing in fear). The longer ending is widely considered a later addition by textual scholars.

Students claim Islam denies Jesus existed, or that Muslims believe Jesus was a mere prophet 'like any other'. Islam affirms Isa as one of the greatest prophets, born of a virgin mother through divine intervention, the Messiah, and raised to heaven by Allah before the crucifixion (Surah 4:157-158 reads 'they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them'). This is a respectful theological position, not a denial of Christianity.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson 1RA0 spec, 4B 2.7 explicitly references Surah 4:157-158 on Isa's death; NATRE guidance on teaching Islam respectfully.

common_misconceptions.topic: Sources of authority in 5-mark Explain questions
common_misconceptions.misconception: Students get the 5-mark Explain question (which requires one source of wisdom or authority) wrong by either omitting the source citation altogether, paraphrasing without attribution, or citing a source that doesn't actually say what they claim. Examiners flag this consistently — the source must be named (e.g. 'In Surah 2:183', 'In Catechism 2360', 'In the Lord's Prayer') and used to support the explanation, not decorate it.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson Edexcel exemplar answer packs (2024 series, both Christianity and Catholic Christianity); Pearson Religious Studies subject updates discuss the 5-mark source-of-wisdom requirement repeatedly.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students develop their own view in depth on a 12-mark Discuss but treat the 'other side' as a single brief sentence ('Christians might disagree because...') with no scriptural anchor or reasoning. Examiners consistently note that the alternative perspective is the weakest point of student responses — it must be developed with the same depth as the main argument and supported by a named source where possible.
common_misconceptions.source: Pearson Edexcel 2024 exemplar answer commentary — 'alternative points of view being brief rather than fully developed and development being more descriptive than explanatory' (qualifications.pearson.com 2024 exemplar packs).

student_errors_by_question_type.3 marks — Outline Three: Students give one extended answer instead of three discrete points. Each of the three must be a separate identifiable point — not three sentences elaborating one idea. Examiners credit the first three discrete points only.
student_errors_by_question_type.4 marks — Explain Two: Students give two points but only briefly state each — no development. 'Explain' demands development 'beyond a habitual response' (Edexcel command-word definition). Two well-developed points beats four undeveloped ones.
student_errors_by_question_type.5 marks — Explain Two with Sources: Students offer two points but only one source, or no clear source, or a vague paraphrase 'the Bible says we should love our neighbour' without naming a specific reference. The 5th mark depends on the source being identifiable (book, surah, named teaching, named Catechism paragraph, named hadith).
student_errors_by_question_type.12 marks — Discuss a Statement: Three common failure modes: (1) the alternative point of view is underdeveloped, (2) the conclusion restates rather than evaluates, (3) the argument relies on opinion without scriptural or doctrinal backing. The best 12-mark answers present 2-3 developed reasons on each side, weigh them explicitly, and reach a justified judgement. SPaG marks are additional (3 marks on selected questions) — students often forget terminology that earns SPaG.

topic_weighting_notes: Paper 1 (50%) is twice the weighting of any other single paper. Beliefs and Practices content is heavily examined; Sources of Wisdom and Forms of Expression sections sometimes appear as the 5-mark or 12-mark questions in Paper 1 question (c) or (d). Don't shortchange those sections.

Within each Paper 1/2 religion, the comparison-marked spec points (1.x* and 2.x* — e.g. Catholic 1.8 eschatology, 2.2 liturgical worship) consistently anchor the 12-mark Discuss questions because they explicitly require comparison with another tradition.

Paper 4 (Textual Studies) is the unfamiliar option for most students — fewer schools teach it than Paper 3 (Philosophy & Ethics). Make Paper 4 content welcoming and explicit about the named passages, because students will rely heavily on these lessons.

Pope Francis (Not Just Good But Beautiful, Evangelii Gaudium), Humanae Vitae (Paul VI), Familiaris Consortio (John Paul II) are the Edexcel-named papal documents — Catholic students must know what each one teaches and which pope wrote it.
Surah anchors and Catechism paragraph numbers appear repeatedly in 5-mark Explain questions because they fulfil the 'named source' requirement. Build them into key-facts boxes.
current_spec_changes: Edexcel 1RA0 Issue 2 (January 2024): topic references (e.g. 1A, 1B) and section names added throughout the spec; the definition of 'evaluate' in the command-word taxonomy was updated to align better with the updated 2024 mark schemes. Mark schemes were amended; first assessment under amended level descriptors was Summer 2024. Source: Pearson Edexcel 1RA0 specification Issue 2, page 1 ('Summary of changes').
pedagogical_notes: EEF research on retrieval practice (educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk): retrieval of incorrect information embeds misconceptions, so feedback must address misconceptions before adding new material. For RS, this means the knowledge-check questions must surface and explicitly correct common factual errors (wrong scripture cited, wrong attribution of theological position, conflated denominational stance), not just test recall.

EEF guidance on diagnostic assessment: anticipate likely misconceptions and use diagnostic probes early in a topic. For RS this maps onto the 'common misconceptions' list above — each one should be a deliberate prompt in either a key-fact, a knowledge check, or a glossary term, not a one-off correction.

NATRE guidance on teaching about Islam: 25% of UK teachers report low confidence teaching Islam. Avoid 'textbook Islam' that focuses purely on doctrine — show lived practice, diversity within Sunni/Shi'a/Sufi, and avoid stereotype-reinforcing imagery (the 'Picturing Islam' resource shows the diversity problem clearly).

RE Today / NATRE: comparison and contrast skills benefit from explicit scaffolding — Venn diagrams, paired-paragraph writing with model amendment. For Edexcel's 12-mark Discuss this maps directly: students need a structural template for handling the comparison side of the argument.

Theos Think Tank (theosthinktank.co.uk): the shift from 'theological' to 'sociological' framing in RE has trade-offs — students can lose sight of religion as a normative framework. For Edexcel RS, this means presenting beliefs as believers hold them, not just describing them externally. Maintain DfE political-impartiality guidance throughout — present divergent positions fairly without endorsing.

Pearson Edexcel 2024 exemplar packs (Christianity and Catholic Christianity): the strongest 12-mark answers do three things — develop both sides with named sources, weigh them explicitly using evaluative connectives, and close with a justified conclusion that picks a side. The weakest ones list points without weighing, leave the alternative view as a one-line concession, or conclude with 'it is a matter of personal opinion'.

gaps: Edexcel 4B 2.5 lists the Prophet Dawud's writing of the Zabur (Psalms) — the Zabur is real, the Psalms in the Hebrew Bible are attributed to David in Jewish tradition. We cover it accurately as Islamic teaching about Dawud receiving the Zabur as scripture; we do not claim historical authorship.

Edexcel 4A 2.8 specifies one of three named figures (Bonhoeffer, Romero, Mother Teresa) as the modern discipleship example. We cover all three so students can choose; the content agent should give all three roughly equal depth.

Edexcel 1.x.* and 2.x.* starred comparison points (e.g. 1A 1.8*, 1A 2.2*, 1B 1.6*, 1B 2.1*, 1C 1.8*, 1C 2.3*) explicitly require comparison with another religion's view. We do not include comparison content as separate lessons — the content agent must surface 'comparison with [other tradition]' explicitly in the relevant lesson sections.
